subject: Renewal & scale: proposed commit uplift and tier change for Highwater Labs
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan@highwater.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal proposal — commit uplift and tier change

Jordan —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, Highwater is seeing sustained growth on the recommendation and personalization endpoints. To avoid any throttling and to secure predictable unit economics for Q1, I put together a proposal for a hosted-commit uplift and a slight tier rebanding that should lower your effective per-token cost while preserving burst capacity.

High-level:
- Current monthly commit: 3M tokens
- Proposed monthly commit: 8M tokens (start-of-term increase)
- Rate changes: move from the Standard tier to the Volume II band (see attached ratecard)
- Burst buffer: 25% monthly burst pool for seasonal spikes

Impact and ops:
- Estimated baseline savings: ~22% / token compared to current pay-as-you-go
- Start date target: first invoice cycle after DocuSign sign (we suggested Nov 30)

Attachments: Highwater_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW + MCR), Redwood_Enterprise_Ratecard_Q4.csv

Next steps:
1) Internal approvals on the discount cadence (Vanessa / Ben — I flagged a 6% prepay incentive).
2) Jordan — can you confirm the procurement timeline and whether Highwater will prepay?
3) Legal to review SOW — I included the standard SLA and fallback routing options.

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

—Alex
Alex Martinez | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Price <jordan@highwater.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@highwater.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T11:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — commit uplift and tier change

Alex —

Thanks for the clear proposal. The uplift looks aligned with where we're headed, but a few quick clarifying Qs from procurement & infra:  

- Can you confirm the effective per-token rate at 8M commit vs current? (need line item for budget approval)
- What are the SLA credits if we hit sustained latency >200ms?
- Is the burst pool a hard cap or configurable?

Procurement is aiming for a signed agreement by end of month, but we need a short payment window (Net 30 vs Net 45 conversation). Also looping in our infra lead if you have a runbook for migration of cached prefixes and any recommended warm-up strategies.

Jordan
Jordan Price | Head of Product
Highwater Labs
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal — internal pricing guidance

Alex/Ben —

Quick internal note before we reply to Jordan: Ops is comfortable offering a 6% annual prepay discount on top of the Volume II band for this uplift. We should also include a 30-day grace period for the first month of ramp to account for warm-up traffic; don't promise more on the SLA side than our standard (SLA credit table in ratecard).

Recommend we:
- Lock in 8M monthly commit with 25% burst (configurable, but requires 48h notice for increases >50% sustained).
- Offer Net 45 payment terms if Highwater pre-pays 6 months; otherwise Net 30.
- Provide a brief migration runbook and offer 2 free migration-support hours (customer success).

Ben — can you confirm final rate numbers so Alex can send updated SOW/docu-sign link?

Thanks —V
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan@highwater.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — commit uplift and tier change

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turn. Per internal approvals we can confirm: 

- Effective per-token rate at 8M commit (post 6% prepay incentive) is shown in the attached ratecard; summary: $0.0018 / token for generative endpoints, $0.00085 / vector-embed unit.
- SLA: standard SLA applies (99.9% uptime). SLA credits: see SOW (Highwater_SOW_v2.pdf). We will not change the SLA beyond that.
- Burst pool: configured as a 25% monthly buffer; it is soft-configurable but sustained increases >50% require 48 hours notice and may be subject to throttling or additional commit charges.

I've uploaded an updated SOW (Highwater_SOW_v2.pdf) and the ratecard. Also shared a short migration runbook and an ops checklist in the Drive link. For signatures, DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/xxxxxxxx

If procurement confirms prepay, we can apply the 6% discount and set billing terms to Net 45. If not, default to Net 30 and no additional discount. I attached a procurement-friendly summary you can forward to your finance team.

On the infra side: we'll allocate 2 migration-support hours from our Customer Success team and schedule a checkpoint the week of Nov 29 to validate traffic shaping and KV cache warm-up.

Onward if that works — happy to adjust wording for legal.

—Alex

Alex and team —

We reviewed the SOW and ratecard with finance and legal. Highwater will sign with the 8M commit and the 25% burst pool. Procurement confirmed they will prepay 6 months to get the 6% discount; please prepare invoice and updated DocuSign reflecting Net 45. 

Requested start date: Nov 30. Please confirm Customer Success checkpoint and share the migration runbook link. Also confirm who will be the day-of contact for throttling incidents.

We'll countersign as soon as DocuSign is updated. Great work getting this over the line.

Best —Jordan
